newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil slides again as US gasoline demand fails.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil slides again as US gasoline demand fails.

text.p: Oil prices looked vulnerable again on Thursday in a market where supplies still easily outweigh sickly demand.
Traders said prices would continue to tread on thin ice until extra demand began to feed through for gasoline to fuel the summer U.S. driving season.
London May Brent futures slipped another six cents a barrel by 1620 GMT to $17.69 a barrel, a fresh nine-month low after a recovery lost steam on Wednesday.
"After the failure to stay above $18 yesterday things are beginning to look a little dangerous again for this market," said a trader in London.
"Gasoline has proved disappointing so far. There's no sign yet of any concerns over a shortage of gasoline in the U.S..." the trader said.
Dealers pointed to the upward spiral of Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food exchange as a key factor undermining prices.
Iraqi sales are now thought to be running somewhere near 800,000 barrels a day (bpd), up from just over 500,000 bpd early in the year.
The extra sales are needed for Baghdad to meet a permitted $2 billion target by the end of June.
The United Nations on Wednesday approved a further four oil sale contracts and now has authorised a total of 44 contracts worth a total $16 billion.
Oil markets are unlikely to get any help from oil producers group OPEC.

The president of the 11-strong Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), Libyan oil minister Abdalla el-Badri, has been consulting this week with his ministerial counterparts about the oil price weakness.
But OPEC sources and delegates say the group, pumping almost two million bpd above its self-imposed 25.03 million ceiling, will do nothing to rein in production.
Dealers said there was no sign yet that the financial funds which baled out of oil in recent weeks would be tempted back into the market by the lower prices.
